Question: Can a collar hurt my anxious dog?
Answer: Yes, a collar can hurt your “anxious” dog. “Traditional collars can harm a dog's neck if it pulls hard on the leash or if a pet owner uses the collar to pull the dog around. ... Repeated stress on the neck can even lead to long-term medical issues—including damaging the thyroid glands and tissues around the neck area and salivary glands” 5 Ways Collars Can Harm Your Dog | PetMD Were I you, I would strongly consider getting my dog a harness. Yes, a harness: One that fits my dog perfectly, is soft and comfortable, and that can be worn whenever we go out together or, in fact, all the time. Then, I would use this harness to train my dog and myself how to use a leash. Here are three harness suggestions (all less than $20) that I would consider: Amazon.com : Voyager Step-in Air Dog Harness - All Weather Mesh, Step in Vest Harness for Small and Medium Dogs by Best Pet Supplies : Pet Supplies Amazon.com : Authentic Puppia Soft Dog Harness, Red - Medium : Pet Leashes : Pet Supplies Amazon.com : Bolux Dog Harness, No-Pull Reflective Breathable Adjustable Pet Vest with Handle for Outdoor Walking - No More Pulling, Tugging or Choking : Pet Supplies Your dog loves and wants to please you. Love your dog and show your dog just what needs to be done for you two to have fun together. Make learning fun! Here’s some advice from the AKC: Leash Train Your Puppy In 5 Easy Steps I would buy myself a matching leash that fit comfortably in my hand and was about 6′ long (so I could walk with my dog on my left side, with the handle of the leash held gently in my right hand and the leash draping across my front to be held in my left hand — to safely control my dog). With this set up, I would practice proper use of a leash. Any needed correction is made with a “quick snap and instant release” — a light, attention-getting “pop” — this takes practice to learn to do easily, gently and quick, quick. I would use my dog’s collar and our leash — along with a pocketful of dog kibble to use as treats, plus lots and lots of praise and petting — to teach “Come” and much more, gently and easily. Yes, I use voice commands. I also say my dog’s name first, then the command. I use “Good girl” and “Go free” (as a release so my dog knows she has done what I asked). I walk my dog with my dog by my left side and our leash held gently in my left hand (Again, with the leash draped across my front, so the handle is held in my right hand.) I first sit her on my left. (To “sit” her, stand with her to your left, at your side, then hold the leash down with your left hand, while offering a treat with your right — coming from in front of her eyes, then back over and above her head, saying “Trixie, sit” as she does so. With your left hand, guide and follow her down and back. Give her the treat. Good girl.) If we are just going for a walk — not at heel — I say “Trixie, let’s go.” Generally, I talk with her as we walk along together. If we are going to be “at heel” — I say “Trixie, heel” and step out on my left foot (on her side, so she can easily see my left leg and foot). We may go a few steps, then I may choose to “sit” her again. What we do is up to me. I am always in control. She is always safe when she is with me. See? Buy yourself a harness and a leash and have fun with your dog. Teach your dog with love and slowly eliminate the treats because you always have your gentle, happy voice and your petting with you, so you can reward yourself and your dog. Wishing you and yours stay safe, healthy and happy, Leslie

Question: Do you have to pay for a dog microchip every year?
Answer: Buying the chip is a one-time deal: ABOUT MICROCHIPPING: You need to have your dog microchipped and record the number. Were I doing this, I would get my dog microchipped by our vet. Your pet’s microchip number also needs to be registered. For $25 US, you can buy a complete kit: Register your pet as instructed by the microchip manufacturer. The American Kennel Club offers “AKC Reunite”: Offering both microchips and lifetime registration (Lifetime enrollment is $19.50 online). An AKC chip including registration with AKC Reunite is about $35.

Question: How would a Jamaican person react if a big dog snuck up behind them out of nowhere and licked their face?
Answer: Whether a person is from Jamaica or not doesn’t seem to make much difference to me: A dog sneaking up behind a person for a “surprise lick” without permission is intolerable. If this were a game the two (dog licker and the lickee) were playing, then that’s one thing — although this seems most improbable — but a surprise attack is downright aggression. Whether the dog is a giant (like our English mastiffs) or a toy poodle, jumping up on, licking anyone without permission makes the dog be impolite and unwelcome in society. “Without permission” is the key here. Would I permit this? No. But some folks would enjoy being jumped on and kissed. Were my friend the owner of the “jump and kiss” dog, I would tell my friend that I do not want “jump and kiss” because it’s rude. I do not want paw prints and slobber on me or my clothes. I do not want to be forced to discipline another person’s dog. This is not the dog’s fault: It is the owner’s responsibility. I likely would suggest that letting me come inside and sit down comfortably before the “jump and kiss” dog was let in might be a viable option. It also may be that the owner is going to continue to make the “jump and kiss” dog unpopular and unwelcome. If so, then my visit to this friend’s house would be a twofer: Two visits in one, first and last. So be it.

Question: What's the best food to feed my Bernese Mountain Dog?
Answer: We believe in dry dog food, which we use as treats as well as food. Dry dog food — softened with warm tap water and with something nice on top (like canned puppy food or canned chicken or tuna, etc.) — works perfectly for pups/dogs of every age. “Made in China” is a serious negative, so for us this eliminates “Royal Canin” and many more: Dog Food Made in China – Controversy, Melamine, Risks, Brands & FAQs This is also why we do not ever feed our dogs any treats made by any manufacturer: Dogs have died from “treats” and pig ears and such. Skip all of this! Instead, give your pup pieces of apple, carrots, frozen green peas, cooked and sliced sweet potato, etc. (We also keep small containers of our dogs’ dry dog food available to use as “treats” — our dogs view these “kibbles” as special and delightful, while we view their kibbles as safe, easy to keep on hand, fresh, and totally trustworthy. For us, it’s win, win!) We start our pups on the same food that they will eat for the rest of their lives, simply moving from puppy to grown dog to senior, as their lives progress. We live in the USA, so we are able to feed our dogs Fromm’s Large Breed Puppy Gold Dog Food (a Wisconsin-made dog food by folks we trust). Fromm’s does not sell to places like PetSmart and other big box pet food stores, but is available at most good private pet stores and is shipped by Fromm’s to our house. (Our English mastiffs — pictured at the bottom of this answer — have been fed Fromm’s all their lives.) Two other brands that I have found to be both good-quality and readily available American brands are IAMS PROACTIVE HEALTH Smart Puppy Large Breed Dry Dog Food Chicken, 15 lb. Bag - Walmart.com and Purina ONE Natural Large Breed Dry Puppy Food, SmartBlend Formula, 16.5 lb. Bag - Walmart.com (FYI: Walmart’s “Old Roy” is not recommended.) Before we found Fromm’s, we have fed Iams and Purina: Both are long-standing brands here in this country, consequently I presume them to be trustworthy. (I have serious doubts about “designer dogs” and “designer dog foods”: Both to me seem to appeal more to one’s ego, than to reason and worth.) Of all the American brands, at the very top of my list is Fromm’s because I know I can trust these folks. I will never choose to feed my dogs anything else. If I lived in Europe or Asia, I would feed “Happy Dog” because of its long history of European manufacture: “From Wehringen (Grermany) to the world: We export our products to over 70 countries on 3 continents.” All you feed is love - it's the most important ingredient in our food These are our two English mastiffs: Trixie is 8, has a trim figure, a healthy body, and looks to have a long life ahead, while Shomer is still a puppy who will grow to weigh about 175-pounds (Trixie is about 150-pounds). Both have been fed Fromm’s. Both are thriving and happy, happy. Wishing you and your dog every joy!

Question: What is the best fabric to use on furniture for dog owners?
Answer: We have had great luck with microfiber and “faux” leather because both of these can be wiped off/spot-cleaned successfully. We buy “leather” seats for our cars and RVs. We chose “microfiber” — man-made, suede-looking stuff — for our couches and chairs. All of this stuff has lasted 10+ years and still looks good, good. We have an upholstered chair — heavy fabric, scotch-guarded, etc. — that we have given up on because the dogs love it, sit on it and are always “doggie wonderful” with hair and drool, etc. It is now “the dog’s chair.” Oops! Wishing you and yours stay safe, healthy and happy, Leslie
